text: Chapter 1 established why security has to move earlier in the pipeline. Chapter 2 asks the question that sits underneath almost every other security control: who, or what, is allowed to do anything at all? This lesson introduces Identity and Access Management, and the single principle that should guide every access decision Northbridge Retail's platform team makes: least privilege.

IAM answers two questions for every request: who or what is making it, and what are they allowed to do. At Northbridge Retail, that who includes engineers signing into the Azure portal, the checkout service calling the payments API, and the CI/CD pipeline deploying a new container image. Every one of those is a principal, and least privilege means each gets exactly the access its job requires — no more. Not access that seems close enough, not whatever the last person in the role had, and not admin because it's simpler than figuring out the real requirement.

An identity's privilege level determines its blast radius: how much damage is possible if it's ever compromised, misused, or simply makes a mistake. A read-only reporting credential that leaks is a bounded problem — an attacker can view data, nothing more. A broadly-scoped admin credential that leaks can mean deleted infrastructure, exfiltrated customer data, or a planted backdoor. Most real breaches don't start with a broken encryption algorithm — they start with a credential that had more access than its job required.

At Northbridge, a database administrator gets access scoped to the databases they manage, not every subscription in the tenant. The checkout service's identity can read the one Key Vault secret it needs, nothing else in that vault. The pipeline deploying the inventory service can deploy that service, not modify IAM roles or touch unrelated resource groups. Every technology the rest of this chapter covers — Azure RBAC, AWS IAM, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity — is a mechanism for implementing this same principle. Next up: Microsoft Entra ID and Azure RBAC.
